name: Harness
purpose: one runtime that runs every department's agents well, on members' own models, with the same quality as Claude Code or Codex.
exit_gate: harness eval suite at its pass^k bar; budget and loop kill tests pass.
traps: do not split one piece of work across writer, tester and reviewer agents; do not put timestamps in the prompt prefix.
note: `passes` is set only by CI after a task's acceptance tests pass there. Dependencies default to the previous task in the phase; loosen them when tasks are independent. Areas are a first guess; one agent per area at a time.

tasks.title: Model router: sources are CLIs and API keys, chosen by task type, capability, data scope and headroom; every choice to the decision log.
spec_refs: README: Core runtime (harness), all subsections. Section 11.10.
acceptance: harness eval suite at pass^3 0.70; budget kill and loop kill; a run resumed after a crash continues from its checkpoint; prompt prefix stays byte-identical across steps (cache test); decomposability chooses single-agent for sequential tasks in the eval. A coding agent cannot run a shell command, reach the network, use its own MCP servers or push without a member decision; a tainted run asks before every push even with a standing rule; every permission decision appears in `run_steps` and the audit log.

tasks.title: Coding tasks go to the provider's own coding agent through its runner, wrapped in our context, leases, approvals and evaluator. The runner starts the CLI in its most restrictive permission mode, maps its permission requests to Library approvals, applies the member's standing rules, and turns on the provider's OS sandbox where one exists (README: Coding agents' own tools).
